articles.title: French skipper wins Route du Rhum
articles.description: French sailor Tom Laperche has won the Route du Rhum, setting a new record in the transatlantic yacht race. The 29-year-old crossed the finish line in Guadeloupe on his first attempt, beating the previous 2022 record by around six hours. A remarkable debut in one of sailing's toughest competitions!

articles.title: Poland in shock after 6 killed in Krakow far-right shooting
articles.description: Poland on Sunday launched a terror probe into the mass shooting in Krakow the day before, in which six people were killed and many more were injured. Authorities have said that the 24-year-old suspect, who used a semi-automatic rifle in his killing spree, was “fascinated by far-right ideologies”. He is currently in critical condition in hospital. FRANCE 24 journalist Adrien Sariat reports from Poland.

articles.title: Middle East live: Israeli president officially tasks Eisenkot with forming government
articles.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Sunday officially tasked ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that or incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won a clear majority in Israel's October 28 elections. Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to form a coalition government. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments from the Middle East.

articles.title: Donald Trump wants UFC fighters as assistants
articles.description: After a series of combative press briefings between the Trump administration and journalists, the US president surprised many by reportedly offering Dana White, the head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) and a longtime friend, the role of White House press secretary. Trump praised White as a “violent fighter and warrior”, but US media reports say he has already turned down the offer. Was it a punchy choice by the president or simply a punchline? Jack Pownall takes a closer look.

articles.title: En Europe, la menace d’une lassitude grandissante des citoyens à l’égard de la guerre en Ukraine
articles.description: Les Européens sont majoritairement convaincus que la Russie constitue une menace pour le Vieux Continent, et continuent à soutenir Kiev. Cependant, à l’heure où le pouvoir d’achat des ménages est rogné par l’inflation, le coût de l’aide militaire à Kiev est de plus en plus montré du doigt, notamment par les partis d’extrême droite ou au sein de la gauche radicale.

articles.title: Europe will take part in US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, French FM says
articles.description: France will participate in the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on ending the Ukraine war, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Sunday, adding that Europeans will be represented at the summit. The talks will take place under US mediation on Tuesday and Wednesday.

articles.title: Israel's Arab-led parties gain influence
articles.description: Arab-led parties have endorsed Gadi Eisenkot despite his ruling out a coalition with them. Their support is driven by a shared goal: removing Benjamin Netanyahu from power. But could these parties ultimately hold the balance of power in forming Israel's next government? Antonia Kerrigan reports.

articles.title: Gaza: Heavy rain inundates thousands of tents
articles.description: Heavy rainfall has flooded thousands of tents sheltering displaced Palestinians across the Gaza Strip, including in Deir al-Balah. Residents say overflowing sewage has mixed with the floodwater, further worsening already dire living conditions. Families are struggling to salvage their belongings, building makeshift earthen barriers and trying to drain the water by hand. Many have seen essential items soaked and rendered unusable, adding to the hardship faced by those already displaced.

articles.title: La mission d'Israël en Iran n'est "pas terminée", prévient le ministre de la Défense

articles.title: Des centaines de milliers d'Ukrainiens sans électricité après des frappes russes

articles.description: Depuis le début de l'année, les arrestations et les exécutions se sont multipliées dans le pays, en lien avec les manifestations antigouvernementales, puis la guerre déclenchée en février par des frappes israélo-américaines contre Téhéran.

articles.title: New Zealand's knife-edge parliamentary election delivers no clear winner
articles.description: No clear winner was produced in New Zealand’s legislative elections Saturday, setting up the two main blocs – Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition and opposition leader Chris Hipkins' left-wing alliance – for weeks of political wrangling to attempt to cobble together a majority. Hipkins said that while New Zealanders had spoken, "it may take us a little bit longer to figure out exactly what it is that you've said".

articles.title: En Espagne, Pedro Sanchez tente de relancer sa campagne après la catastrophe ferroviaire d’Urda
